course.title: Smoothie and Juice Making
course.tagline: Blend fresh smoothies and juices, and turn it into a small business.

days.title: Smoothie Basics: What You Need
days.goal: Know your tools and the parts of a good smoothie.
steps: Find your tools: a blender, a knife, a chopping board, and cups.
A smoothie has four parts: fruit, liquid, something creamy, and something extra.
Fruit gives flavour and sweetness. Use ripe fruit.
Liquid can be water, milk, or yoghurt.
Something creamy like banana or yoghurt makes it thick and smooth.
days.task: List your tools and make your first simple smoothie: banana, milk, and honey.
days.challenge: Taste it and write down what you would change.

quiz.q: What are the four parts of a smoothie?
quiz.explain: Fruit, liquid, something creamy, and something extra make a good smoothie.

quiz.q: Why use ripe fruit?
options: Ripe fruit is sweeter and softer
quiz.explain: Ripe fruit is sweet and blends smoothly.

quiz.q: What makes a smoothie thick?
quiz.explain: Banana and yoghurt make a smoothie thick and creamy.

days.title: Your First Fruit Smoothie
days.goal: Blend a simple fruit smoothie.

video.title: How to Make Fruit Smoothies | Smoothie Recipes

steps: Pick two fruits: banana and mango work well.
Peel and chop the fruit into small pieces.
Add the fruit to the blender with milk or water.
Blend for 1 minute until smooth. Stop and check.
Pour into a glass and taste. Add honey if you want it sweeter.
days.task: Blend a banana and mango smoothie.
days.challenge: Blend a second smoothie with different fruit and compare.

quiz.q: Why chop fruit small before blending?
options: Small pieces blend faster and smoother
quiz.explain: Small pieces blend quickly and give a smooth drink.

quiz.q: How long should you blend a smoothie?
quiz.explain: About 1 minute is enough for a smooth blend.

quiz.q: What can you add if a smoothie is not sweet enough?
quiz.explain: Honey or ripe banana adds sweetness naturally.

days.title: Mango Smoothies: Three Ways
days.goal: Make three different mango smoothies.
steps: Mango and banana: sweet and creamy.
Mango and pineapple: fresh and sharp.
Mango and greens: mango with spinach or kale.
Taste each one and note the colour, taste, and thickness.
Pick your favourite and write the recipe down.
days.task: Make three mango smoothies.
days.challenge: Serve the best one to a friend and ask what they think.

quiz.q: What does pineapple add to a mango smoothie?
quiz.explain: Pineapple adds a fresh, sharp taste that balances the sweet mango.

quiz.q: Can you taste spinach in a green smoothie?
options: Barely, if you use enough sweet fruit
quiz.explain: Sweet fruit like mango covers the taste of spinach.

quiz.q: Why write down your favourite recipe?
options: So you can make it again the same way
quiz.explain: A written recipe lets you repeat a good smoothie.

days.title: Green Smoothies: Healthy and Tasty
days.goal: Make a green smoothie that actually tastes good.
steps: Green smoothies use leafy greens like spinach or kale.
Use more fruit than greens: two parts fruit to one part greens.
Add a banana for sweetness and creaminess.
Add water or coconut water as the liquid.
Blend for 1 to 2 minutes until no green bits are left.
days.task: Make a green smoothie with spinach, banana, and mango.
days.challenge: Make a second one with kale and compare the taste.

quiz.q: How much fruit should a green smoothie have?
options: More fruit than greens, about two to one
quiz.explain: Two parts fruit to one part greens keeps it sweet and tasty.

quiz.q: Why add banana to a green smoothie?
quiz.explain: Banana sweetens the smoothie and makes it thick.

quiz.q: How long should you blend a green smoothie?
quiz.explain: Greens need longer blending to disappear fully.

days.title: Energy Smoothies: For Busy Days
days.goal: Make smoothies that give you energy.
steps: Energy smoothies add oats, peanut butter, or nuts.
Oats make a smoothie filling, so you stay full longer.
Peanut butter adds protein and a rich taste.
Add a banana and milk for a breakfast smoothie.
Drink it in the morning or before a workout.
days.task: Make an energy smoothie with oats and peanut butter.
days.challenge: Make a breakfast smoothie and drink it instead of your usual breakfast.

quiz.q: What do oats add to a smoothie?
options: They make it filling so you stay full longer
quiz.explain: Oats add fibre, which keeps you full for longer.

quiz.q: What does peanut butter add?
quiz.explain: Peanut butter adds protein and a rich, nutty taste.

quiz.q: When is a good time for an energy smoothie?
options: In the morning or before a workout
quiz.explain: Energy smoothies are best in the morning or before exercise.

days.title: Juice Basics: Fresh Juice at Home
days.goal: Make fresh juice without a juicer.
steps: You can make juice with a blender and a strainer.
Chop fruit and blend it with a little water.
Pour through a fine strainer or a clean cloth.
Press the pulp with a spoon to get all the juice out.
Drink it fresh. Juice loses vitamins if it sits too long.
days.task: Make fresh orange or pineapple juice with a blender and strainer.
days.challenge: Make a mixed fruit juice and compare the taste.

quiz.q: How do you make juice without a juicer?
quiz.explain: Blend the fruit with a little water, then strain out the pulp.

quiz.q: Why strain the juice?
options: To remove the pulp and make it smooth
quiz.explain: Straining removes pulp and leaves smooth juice.

quiz.q: Why drink juice fresh?
options: Juice loses vitamins if it sits too long
quiz.explain: Fresh juice has the most vitamins. It drops the longer it sits.

days.title: Week 1 Project: A Smoothie Menu
days.goal: Make a menu of three smoothies and serve them.
steps: Pick three smoothies: a fruit one, a green one, and an energy one.
Write the recipes with exact amounts.
Buy all the fruit in one trip.
Make all three and taste them with your household.
Pick the best one and name it.
days.task: Make three smoothies and serve them as a menu.
days.challenge: Ask everyone to vote for their favourite.

quiz.q: Why make three different smoothies?
options: It shows your range and lets people choose
quiz.explain: A menu with three choices shows your skill and gives people options.

quiz.q: Why write recipes with exact amounts?
options: So you can make them the same way every time
quiz.explain: Exact amounts mean the same great taste every time.

quiz.q: Why name your best smoothie?
options: A name makes it easy to sell and remember
quiz.explain: A named smoothie is a product you can sell.

project.title: Make a Three-Smoothie Menu
project.brief: Make a fruit smoothie, a green smoothie, and an energy smoothie.

days.title: Cold-Pressed Juice: The Slow Way
days.goal: Make cold-pressed juice and learn why it is special.
steps: Cold-pressed means juice pressed slowly without heat.
No heat means more vitamins stay in the juice.
Use a juicer if you have one, or a blender and strainer.
Press the fruit slowly. Do not rush it.
Store in a sealed bottle in the fridge and drink within 2 days.
days.task: Make a cold-pressed style juice with a blender and strainer.
days.challenge: Make a green power juice with cucumber, apple, and greens.

quiz.q: What does cold-pressed mean?
quiz.explain: Cold-pressed juice is pressed slowly without heat.

quiz.q: Why is cold-pressed juice special?
options: No heat means more vitamins stay in
quiz.explain: Heat destroys vitamins. Cold pressing keeps more of them.

quiz.q: How long does fresh juice keep in the fridge?
quiz.explain: Fresh juice is best within 2 days.

days.title: Pineapple and Mint Juice
days.goal: Make a fresh pineapple and mint juice.
steps: Peel and chop a ripe pineapple.
Add a small handful of fresh mint leaves.
Blend with a little water, then strain.
Taste it. Add a little lime juice for a fresh kick.
Serve cold over ice.
days.task: Make pineapple and mint juice.
days.challenge: Make a second batch with ginger and compare.

quiz.q: What does mint add to juice?
quiz.explain: Mint adds a cool, fresh taste.

quiz.q: What does lime juice add?
quiz.explain: Lime adds a sharp, fresh taste that lifts the juice.

quiz.q: Why serve juice over ice?
quiz.explain: Cold juice is more refreshing, especially on a hot day.

days.title: Grape Juice and Other Fruit Juices
days.goal: Make grape juice and try other fruits.

video.title: How to Make Cold-Pressed Juice Without a Juicer

steps: Wash grapes well and remove the stems.
Blend with a little water, then strain.
Taste it. Grapes are sweet, so you may not need sugar.
Try watermelon juice: blend and strain the same way.
Try a mixed juice: grape and apple.
days.task: Make grape juice.
days.challenge: Make watermelon juice and compare.

quiz.q: Why wash grapes well?
options: To remove dirt and chemicals from the skin
quiz.explain: Washing removes dirt and anything sprayed on the fruit.

quiz.q: Do you need sugar in grape juice?
quiz.explain: Grapes are naturally sweet, so sugar is often not needed.

quiz.q: How do you make watermelon juice?
options: Blend and strain it like other fruit juice
quiz.explain: Watermelon blends and strains the same way as other fruit.

days.title: Smoothie Bowls: Eat Your Smoothie
days.goal: Make a smoothie bowl with toppings.
steps: A smoothie bowl is a thick smoothie served in a bowl.
Use less liquid and more frozen fruit so it is thick.
Pour into a bowl.
Top with sliced fruit, oats, nuts, or seeds.
Eat with a spoon. It is a meal, not a drink.
days.task: Make a smoothie bowl.
days.challenge: Make a second bowl with different toppings.

quiz.q: What makes a smoothie bowl thick?
options: Less liquid and more frozen fruit
quiz.explain: Less liquid and frozen fruit make a thick, spoonable smoothie.

quiz.q: What goes on top of a smoothie bowl?
options: Sliced fruit, oats, nuts, or seeds
quiz.explain: Toppings add crunch, flavour, and make it a full meal.

quiz.q: Why eat a smoothie bowl with a spoon?
options: It is too thick to drink
quiz.explain: A thick smoothie bowl is eaten, not drunk.

days.title: Detox and Cleansing Drinks
days.goal: Make light, fresh drinks with cucumber and lemon.
steps: Detox drinks are light drinks with lots of water and fresh ingredients.
Use cucumber, lemon, mint, and ginger.
Blend with water and strain, or infuse in water overnight.
Drink in the morning for a fresh start.
Keep it simple. No sugar needed.
days.task: Make a cucumber and lemon drink.
days.challenge: Make a ginger and lemon drink and compare.

quiz.q: What is in a detox drink?
options: Cucumber, lemon, mint, and ginger in water
quiz.explain: Detox drinks use fresh ingredients like cucumber, lemon, and ginger in water.

quiz.q: What does ginger add?
quiz.explain: Ginger adds a warm, spicy taste.

quiz.q: Why no sugar in a detox drink?
options: The drink is meant to be light and fresh
quiz.explain: Detox drinks are light and fresh, so they skip sugar.

days.title: Smoothies for Kids and Families
days.goal: Make smoothies the whole family will love.
steps: Use sweet fruit like banana, mango, and berries.
Add milk or yoghurt for a creamy taste.
Let kids pick the fruit and help blend.
Use fun cups and straws.
Keep it sweet and simple. No bitter greens for kids.
days.task: Make a family smoothie and serve it to everyone.
days.challenge: Let a child pick the fruit and make the smoothie with you.

quiz.q: What fruit do kids like best in smoothies?
options: Sweet fruit like banana and mango
quiz.explain: Sweet fruit like banana and mango are kid favourites.

quiz.q: Why let kids help make smoothies?
options: They are more likely to drink what they helped make
quiz.explain: Kids enjoy food more when they helped make it.

quiz.q: Why skip bitter greens for kids?
quiz.explain: Bitter greens can put kids off smoothies.

days.title: Week 2 Project: A Juice Bar Menu
days.goal: Make a juice bar menu with smoothies and juices.
steps: Pick the menu: two smoothies and two juices.
Write the recipes with exact amounts and costs.
Buy all the fruit in one trip.
Make all four drinks and serve them in nice cups.
Ask tasters to pick a favourite and set a price for each drink.
days.task: Make a juice bar menu of four drinks.
days.challenge: Price each drink as if you were selling it.

quiz.q: Why include both smoothies and juices?
quiz.explain: A menu with both gives every customer something they like.

quiz.q: Why cost each drink?
options: So you know what to charge and what you earn
quiz.explain: Costing tells you the price and the profit on each drink.

quiz.q: Why serve drinks in nice cups?
options: Good cups make drinks look worth buying
quiz.explain: A nice cup makes a drink look professional and worth the price.

project.title: Make a Juice Bar Menu
project.brief: Make two smoothies and two fresh juices, priced and served.

days.title: Buying Fruit: Fresh and Cheap
days.goal: Buy fruit well for smoothies and juices.

video.title: I've Juiced for 31 Years. This Is the Green Juice I Drink Daily

steps: Buy fruit in season. It is cheaper and tastes better.
Buy ripe fruit for today and unripe fruit for later in the week.
Check for soft spots and mould. Pick firm, heavy fruit.
Buy from the market in bulk for a lower price.
Store fruit in a cool place. Freeze overripe fruit for smoothies.
days.task: Buy fruit for the week and sort it by ripeness.
days.challenge: Freeze overripe bananas for smoothies.

quiz.q: Why buy fruit in season?
options: It is cheaper and tastes better
quiz.explain: Fruit in season is fresh, cheap, and full of flavour.

quiz.q: Why buy unripe fruit too?
options: It ripens during the week so you always have fruit
quiz.explain: Unripe fruit ripens over days, so you have fresh fruit all week.

quiz.q: What do you do with overripe bananas?
quiz.explain: Frozen overripe bananas are perfect for smoothies.

days.title: Storing Fruit and Juice
days.goal: Store fruit and juice so nothing goes to waste.
steps: Keep ripe fruit in the fridge. Keep unripe fruit on the counter.
Cut fruit and store it in sealed containers.
Freeze fruit in bags for smoothies.
Store juice in sealed bottles in the fridge. Drink within 2 days.
Label everything with the date.
days.task: Freeze fruit in bags for the week.
days.challenge: Store a bottle of juice and check it after 2 days.

quiz.q: Where do you keep ripe fruit?
quiz.explain: The fridge slows ripening so ripe fruit lasts longer.

quiz.q: How do you store cut fruit?
quiz.explain: Sealed containers keep cut fruit fresh and stop it drying out.

quiz.q: Why label juice with the date?
options: So you know when it was made and when to drink it by
quiz.explain: A date tells you if the juice is still fresh.

days.title: Costing Smoothies and Juices
days.goal: Work out what each drink costs and what to charge.

video.title: How to Make Fruit Smoothies | Smoothie Recipes

steps: List every ingredient with its price.
Add the cost of the cup, straw, and packaging.
Divide the total by the number of drinks you made.
Charge 2 to 3 times the cost for a profit.
Compare with juice bars near you.
days.task: Cost one smoothie and set its selling price.
days.challenge: Cost one juice the same way.

quiz.q: What is the cost per drink?
options: Total cost divided by the number of drinks
quiz.explain: Cost per drink is the total cost shared across all the drinks you made.

quiz.q: Why charge 2 to 3 times the cost?
options: To cover cups, packaging, and your time, and still make a profit
quiz.explain: The extra covers all the costs beyond fruit and leaves profit.

quiz.q: What else must you add to the cost?
quiz.explain: Cups, straws, and packaging are real costs of every drink.

days.title: Smoothie Business: Your First Stall
days.goal: Plan a small smoothie stall or delivery.
steps: Pick 3 or 4 drinks to sell. Keep the menu small.
Set your prices from your costing work.
Take clear photos of your drinks in good light.
Tell friends and family first. Ask them to share.
Take orders in advance so you buy only what you need.
days.task: Plan your smoothie stall on paper: menu, prices, and costs.
days.challenge: Take photos of your best drinks and show them to three people.

quiz.q: Why keep the menu small?
options: A small menu is easier to make well and cost
quiz.explain: A small menu keeps quality high and costing simple.

quiz.q: Why take orders in advance?
options: So you buy only what you need and waste nothing
quiz.explain: Advance orders mean no waste and no guessing.

quiz.q: Why do photos matter?
options: Clear photos help people decide to buy
quiz.explain: People buy with their eyes first. Good photos sell drinks.

days.title: Smoothies for Weight and Health
days.goal: Make smoothies that are light and healthy.
steps: Use more vegetables and less sweet fruit.
Skip sugar and honey. Use whole fruit for sweetness.
Add protein like yoghurt or nuts to stay full.
Use water instead of milk to cut calories.
Drink a smoothie as a meal, not on top of a meal.
days.task: Make a light green smoothie with no added sugar.
days.challenge: Make a protein smoothie with yoghurt and nuts.

quiz.q: How do you make a smoothie lighter?
options: Use more vegetables and less sweet fruit
quiz.explain: More vegetables and less sweet fruit make a lighter smoothie.

quiz.q: What adds protein to a smoothie?
quiz.explain: Yoghurt and nuts add protein, which keeps you full.

quiz.q: Why drink a smoothie as a meal?
options: A smoothie has enough in it to count as a meal
quiz.explain: A full smoothie has fruit, protein, and fibre, so it can replace a meal.

days.title: Juice Mistakes and Fixes
days.goal: Fix the commonest smoothie and juice problems.
steps: Smoothie is too thick? Add a little liquid and blend again.
Smoothie is too thin? Add more frozen fruit or banana.
Juice is too sour? Add a sweet fruit like mango or banana.
Smoothie tastes bitter? You used too many greens. Add more fruit.
Write down each problem and fix.
days.task: Fix one smoothie problem you have had.
days.challenge: Make a smoothie, taste it, and adjust it three ways.

quiz.q: What do you do if a smoothie is too thick?
options: Add a little liquid and blend again
quiz.explain: A little liquid thins a thick smoothie.

quiz.q: What do you do if a smoothie is too thin?
options: Add more frozen fruit or banana
quiz.explain: Frozen fruit or banana thickens a thin smoothie.

quiz.q: What do you do if juice is too sour?
options: Add a sweet fruit like mango
quiz.explain: Sweet fruit balances sour juice.

days.title: Week 3 Project: A Full Drinks Menu
days.goal: Make a full drinks menu for a small event.
steps: Pick the menu: three smoothies and two juices.
Write the recipes, costs, and prices.
Buy all the fruit in one trip.
Make all five drinks and serve them in nice cups.
Ask guests to vote for their favourite.
days.task: Make a full drinks menu for your household or friends.
days.challenge: Cost the whole menu and work out your profit if you sold it.

quiz.q: Why make five drinks?
options: A full menu shows your range
quiz.explain: Five drinks show you can make a real menu, not just one drink.

quiz.q: Why cost the whole menu?
options: So you know the profit if you sell it
quiz.explain: Costing the menu tells you if the business can make money.

quiz.q: Why ask guests to vote?
options: Votes tell you which drinks sell best
quiz.explain: Votes show you which drinks to keep on your menu.

project.title: Make a Full Drinks Menu
project.brief: Make three smoothies and two juices for a small event.

days.title: Packaging Drinks for Delivery
days.goal: Pack smoothies and juices so they travel well.
steps: Use clean bottles or cups with tight lids.
Fill bottles to the top so there is little air inside.
Label with the drink name, date, and ingredients.
Keep drinks cold in a cooler bag with ice.
Tell the customer to drink within 2 days.
days.task: Pack a smoothie and a juice as if for delivery.
days.challenge: Deliver a drink to someone and ask for feedback.

quiz.q: Why fill bottles to the top?
options: Less air inside keeps juice fresher
quiz.explain: Air makes juice spoil faster. A full bottle keeps it fresh.

quiz.q: Why keep drinks cold during delivery?
options: Cold keeps juice fresh and safe
quiz.explain: Cold drinks stay fresh and safe during delivery.

quiz.q: What should a label say?
quiz.explain: Labels tell the customer what it is, when it was made, and what is in it.

days.title: Seasonal Fruits: What to Use When
days.goal: Use the best fruit for each season.
steps: Mango season: make mango smoothies and juices.
Pineapple season: make pineapple and mint juice.
Orange season: make fresh orange juice.
When fruit is out of season, use frozen fruit.
Keep a list of what fruit is in season each month.
days.task: Write a list of fruits in season now and plan three drinks.
days.challenge: Make a smoothie with frozen fruit and compare the taste.

quiz.q: Why use fruit in season?
options: It is cheaper and tastes better
quiz.explain: Fruit in season is fresh, cheap, and full of flavour.

quiz.q: What do you do when fruit is out of season?
quiz.explain: Frozen fruit is picked ripe and works well in smoothies.

quiz.q: Why keep a seasonal list?
options: So you always know the cheapest, tastiest fruit
quiz.explain: A seasonal list helps you plan a menu that makes money.

days.title: Smoothies for Workouts
days.goal: Make smoothies for before and after workouts.
steps: Before a workout: light smoothie with banana and water.
After a workout: smoothie with protein, like yoghurt or peanut butter.
Add oats after a workout to replace energy.
Drink water too. Smoothies do not replace water.
Keep it simple. Two or three ingredients are enough.
days.task: Make a pre-workout smoothie.
days.challenge: Make a post-workout smoothie with protein.

quiz.q: What is good before a workout?
options: A light smoothie with banana and water
quiz.explain: A light smoothie gives energy without feeling heavy.

quiz.q: What is good after a workout?
options: A smoothie with protein like yoghurt
quiz.explain: Protein after a workout helps muscles recover.

quiz.q: Do smoothies replace water?
options: No, you still need to drink water
quiz.explain: Smoothies are food. You still need plain water.

days.title: Your Signature Smoothie
days.goal: Choose and perfect one smoothie you can make brilliantly.

video.title: How to Make Cold-Pressed Juice Without a Juicer

steps: Pick the smoothie your household loves most from this course.
Write the recipe in your own words with exact amounts.
Make it again, timing every step and noting problems.
Fix the problems and make it once more.
Get someone new to taste it and give honest feedback.
days.task: Make your signature smoothie and write the final recipe down.
days.challenge: Make it for someone new and record what they say.

quiz.q: What is a signature smoothie?
options: A smoothie you can make brilliantly every time
A smoothie with a fancy name
quiz.explain: A signature smoothie is one you have mastered.

quiz.q: Why write the recipe in your own words?
options: So you truly understand it and can repeat it
quiz.explain: Writing it yourself proves you understand each step.

quiz.q: Why get a new person to taste it?
quiz.explain: People who know you may be polite. New tasters are honest.

days.title: Selling Drinks: First Steps
days.goal: Take your first steps toward selling smoothies and juices.
steps: Pick 3 or 4 drinks to sell. Keep the menu small.
Set your prices from your costing work.
Take clear photos of your drinks in good light.
Tell friends and family first. Ask them to share.
Take orders in advance so you buy only what you need.
days.task: Take photos of your best drinks and show them to three people.
days.challenge: Take one real order, even a small one, and deliver it on time.

quiz.q: Why start with only 3 or 4 drinks?
options: A small menu is easier to make well and cost
quiz.explain: A small menu keeps quality high and costing simple.

quiz.q: Why take orders in advance?
options: So you buy only what you need and waste nothing
quiz.explain: Advance orders mean no waste and no guessing.

quiz.q: Why do photos matter?
options: Clear photos help people decide to buy
quiz.explain: People buy with their eyes first. Good photos sell drinks.

days.title: Keeping Records: Orders and Money
days.goal: Keep simple records of your drinks business.
steps: Write down every order: what, how many, who, and when.
Write down what you spent and what you earned.
Work out your profit each week.
Note which drinks sell best and which do not.
Keep your money for drinks separate from your spending money.
days.task: Start a simple order book today, on paper or on your phone.
days.challenge: Work out your profit from one day of selling.

quiz.q: Why write down every order?
options: So nothing is forgotten and you know what to make
quiz.explain: Written orders stop mistakes and show what sells.

quiz.q: What is profit?
options: What is left after costs are taken from what you earned
quiz.explain: Profit is what remains after you pay for fruit, cups, and packaging.

quiz.q: Why keep drinks money separate?
options: So you always know if the business is making money
quiz.explain: Separate money shows the true profit of your business.

days.title: Juice and Smoothie Trends
days.goal: Try new drink ideas and see what customers like.
steps: Try a new fruit combination each week.
Ask customers what flavours they want.
Try a new topping for smoothie bowls.
Watch what other juice bars sell and learn from them.
Keep what works. Drop what does not sell.
days.task: Try a new fruit combination today.
days.challenge: Ask three people what drink flavour they would like to try.

quiz.q: Why try new combinations?
options: New flavours keep customers coming back
quiz.explain: New flavours give customers a reason to return.

quiz.q: Why ask customers what they want?
options: Customers buy what they asked for
quiz.explain: Asking customers tells you what will sell.

quiz.q: Why drop drinks that do not sell?
options: So you do not waste money on fruit nobody wants
quiz.explain: A drink that does not sell wastes fruit and money.

days.title: Revision: The Drinks Maker's Skills Check
days.goal: Revisit the core skills of the course.
steps: Make a smoothie from memory, without the recipe.
Make fresh juice with a blender and strainer.
Name the four parts of a smoothie.
Cost one drink from memory.
List your three strongest drinks and one to improve.
days.task: Make a full drinks menu from memory, no recipe.
days.challenge: Teach one drink from this course to a friend or family member.

quiz.q: What are the four parts of a smoothie?
quiz.explain: Fruit, liquid, something creamy, and something extra.

quiz.q: Why make drinks from memory?
options: It proves you really know the steps
quiz.explain: Making drinks without a recipe shows the skills are truly learned.

quiz.q: Why teach a drink to someone else?
options: Teaching proves you really know it
quiz.explain: If you can teach it, you truly understand it.

days.title: Capstone Prep: Plan Your Final Drinks Menu
days.goal: Plan your capstone drinks menu and gather everything you need.

video.title: I've Juiced for 31 Years. This Is the Green Juice I Drink Daily

steps: Choose your capstone menu: three smoothies and two juices.
Write the full shopping list with costs.
Write the making order, starting with what takes longest.
Check you have every tool and ingredient.
Do a trial run of the hardest drink if you have time.
days.task: Write your complete capstone plan and cost it.
days.challenge: Do a trial run of your hardest capstone drink today.

quiz.q: What should your capstone show?
options: Everything you learned: smoothies, juices, costing, and serving
quiz.explain: The capstone proves the whole course.

quiz.q: Why start with what takes longest?
options: So everything finishes at the same time
quiz.explain: Long tasks start first so all drinks are ready together.

quiz.q: Why do a trial run?
options: To find problems before the real menu
quiz.explain: A trial run finds problems while there is still time to fix them.

capstone.title: The Juice Bar: A Full Menu of Smoothies and Juices
capstone.brief: Open a small juice bar for a day: serve three smoothies and two fresh juices to your household or customers. Cost every drink, pack them neatly, serve them cold and on time, and collect feedback.
checks: Menu planned with recipes, costs, and prices
Three smoothies made smooth and tasty
Two fresh juices made and strained well
Drinks served cold in nice cups or bottles
Labels with drink name, date, and ingredients
Costs worked out and profit known
Feedback collected from at least one person who drank them
deliverables: A photo of your full drinks menu
Your written menu with recipes, costs, and prices
Your making order, starting with what takes longest
Your signature smoothie recipe written in your own words
A short note on what you learned and what you will improve next
